attempts.title: lookup_customer parameter name mismatch: tool spec says 'email' but function expects 'customer_email'

hypothesis.title: lookup_customer parameter name mismatch: tool spec says 'email' but function expects 'customer_email'
hypothesis.root_cause: The TOOL_SPECS definition declares the parameter as 'email', so the LLM calls lookup_customer({"email": "..."}) — but the actual Python function signature is `def lookup_customer(customer_email: str)`. When run_tool unpacks the JSON args dict with **args, it passes `email=...` which doesn't match `customer_email`, causing TypeError every time. This means customer data is never retrieved, so the agent has no plan/status context to apply the priority policy correctly, and the KB search also fails (returning [] for all queries) because the search_kb function does substring matching against article titles/tags but the queries never match.
evidence: task `password` step 2: lookup_customer returned 'ERROR: TypeError: lookup_customer() got an unexpected keyword argument 'email'' (all 6 tasks show this same error)
task `webhooks-pro` step 2: same TypeError on lookup_customer
task `double-charge` steps 2-3: same TypeError repeated
task `past-due` steps 2-3: same TypeError repeated
triage/tools.py:40 defines `def lookup_customer(customer_email: str)` but TOOL_SPECS at line 20 declares parameter name as 'email'

All tasks show kb_article='' because search_kb returns [] — the KB search logic at tools.py:48-52 only matches if query is a substring of title.lower() or in tags, but the agent's natural-language queries never match
hypothesis.fix_plan:
1. In triage/tools.py, rename the `lookup_customer` function parameter from `customer_email` to `email` so it matches the TOOL_SPECS declaration. This fixes the TypeError.
2. Fix the search_kb matching logic to be more robust — currently `q in a['tags']` checks if the entire query string is a substring of the tags string, which will never match multi-word queries. Change it to check if any tag word appears in the query or vice versa (token-level matching). Also add keyword splitting so partial word matches work.
3. Update the SYSTEM prompt to include the priority policy from policy.py so the LLM applies P1/P2/P3 rules correctly (currently the prompt says 'Use P1 only when the customer explicitly says the issue is urgent' which contradicts the actual policy that P2 applies to pro-plan production outages and enterprise customers).
hypothesis.expected_effect: Fixing the parameter name (fix 1) will eliminate all 11 tool_errors and allow customer plan/status to be retrieved, which combined with the corrected priority policy in the prompt (fix 3) should fix correct_priority for password (P3), double-charge (P3), and webhooks-pro (P2). Fixing search_kb matching (fix 2) should allow KB articles to be found, fixing correct_kb_article for all 6 tasks. Together these changes should flip most or all of the 0/6 passing tasks.

attempts.title: SYSTEM prompt priority policy diverges from policy.py, causing billing issues for Pro customers to be mis-classified as P2

hypothesis.title: SYSTEM prompt priority policy diverges from policy.py, causing billing issues for Pro customers to be mis-classified as P2
hypothesis.root_cause: The SYSTEM prompt describes P2 as 'significant impairment affecting production for a Pro or Enterprise customer' which is vague enough that the model classifies a billing/refund issue for a Pro customer as P2. The authoritative policy.py states P2 for a pro customer requires a 'production outage', and 'everything else' is P3. A duplicate charge is not a production outage, so it should be P3. The prompt's wording 'significant impairment' is too broad and doesn't restrict P2 to production outages for Pro customers.
evidence: task double-charge: priority='P2', expected 'P3' — Ana is on 'pro' plan with a billing/refund question, not a production outage
policy.py PRIORITY_POLICY: 'P2: production outage for a pro customer, any issue for an enterprise customer, or a past_due account that cannot pay.'
policy.py PRIORITY_POLICY: 'P3: everything else (free plan questions, how-to questions, sales enquiries).'

prompts.py SYSTEM: 'P2: significant impairment affecting production for a Pro or Enterprise customer, or any issue for an Enterprise customer' — the phrase 'significant impairment' is broader than 'production outage' and the double 'Enterprise' mention obscures the pro-customer restriction
hypothesis.fix_plan: Replace the priority policy section in SYSTEM with the exact wording from policy.py: P1 = production outage or data loss for enterprise; P2 = production outage for a pro customer, any issue for an enterprise customer, or a past_due account that cannot pay; P3 = everything else. This removes the ambiguous 'significant impairment' phrasing and makes clear that billing questions for pro customers are P3.
hypothesis.expected_effect: double-charge task should flip from failed to passed (correct_priority P2->P3). No regression expected on other tasks: outage-enterprise (P1, enterprise outage), webhooks-pro (P2, production webhooks down = production outage for pro), past-due (P2, past_due account), seats-enterprise (P2, any issue for enterprise), password (P3, general question).

hypothesis.title: SYSTEM prompt P2 rule too broad — billing issues for Pro customers incorrectly classified as P2
hypothesis.root_cause: The SYSTEM prompt defines P2 as 'significant impairment affecting production for a Pro or Enterprise customer, OR any issue for an Enterprise customer.' The phrase 'significant impairment' is vague enough that the model classifies a billing dispute (duplicate charge) for a Pro customer as P2. The real policy in policy.py restricts Pro-customer P2 to 'production outage' only, and puts everything else (including billing questions for Pro customers) in P3. The SYSTEM prompt must be updated to match policy.py exactly.
